saints.name: St. Zita
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A humble maidservant of Lucca who made a lifetime of housework a path to holiness…
biography: Zita was born about 1212 in Tuscany and at the age of twelve entered the service of the wealthy Fatinelli family of Lucca, where she remained a household servant for the rest of her life — some forty-eight years. She rose before dawn to pray and to work, gave her own food and even her master's goods to the poor, and bore the early jealousy of the other servants with patience until her goodness won them over.

Many stories of her charity and of small marvels attending it spread through Lucca, and she was venerated as a saint immediately upon her death in 1272. Her cult was confirmed in 1696, and she is honoured as the patron of domestic workers and servants.
saints.knownFor: Sanctifying humble domestic service through charity and prayer.

canonization.canonized: Cult confirmed 1696 by Pope Innocent XII

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 April
